employeeInputs.source: DR 0004 Line 2 or W-4 filing-status default

steps: annualReduction = DR 0004 Line 2, including zero, when supplied; otherwise 11000 for married filing jointly or qualifying surviving spouse and 5500 for all other W-4 filing statuses
certificatePrecedence: A submitted DR 0004 controls Lines 2 and 3, including an explicit zero.
Without DR 0004, use the W-4 filing-status default.
A W-4 claiming exemption produces zero withholding unless the Department adjusts the claim.
Without either certificate, use the single-status 5500 annual reduction.
calculation.certificateReplacementRule: A new W-4 without a new DR 0004 revokes the prior DR 0004 and any pre-2022 additional-withholding request.
calculation.separateSupplementalMethodStatus: No distinct supplemental-wage method was located in the captured 2026 worksheet.

rounding.officialWorkbookFormulaBehavior: The workbook contains no ROUND function. It retains full precision through annualization, the 4.40% multiplication, deannualization, and addition of extra withholding.
rounding.operationalRule: Calculate all steps at decimal precision and round the final nonnegative withholding amount to the nearest whole dollar for the displayed and posted payroll result.

workbookDerivedRegressionCases.name: Biweekly explicit zero reduction and additional withholding

residencyAndWorkRules.residentRule: Withhold from federally taxable Colorado wages paid to a Colorado resident whether the work is performed inside or outside Colorado.
residencyAndWorkRules.nonresidentRule: Withhold from federally taxable wages paid to a nonresident for services physically performed in Colorado.

filing.frequencySelectionBasis: Total annual Colorado wage withholding liability

frequencyThresholds.due: Last day of the month following the calendar quarter

frequencyThresholds.annualWithholding: At least $7,000 but not more than $50,000

frequencyThresholds.due: Third business day following the Friday that concludes the week

filing.exactlyFiftyThousandAmbiguity: The January 2026 guide includes exactly $50,000 in both the monthly and weekly rows; do not assign this boundary automatically until the Department supplies a tie-break or account assignment.

captureWarnings: Colorado rejected automated direct retrieval of the official files with HTTP 403; the manually downloaded PDF, guide, certificate, and calculator workbook are now checksummed.

The official workbook resolves calculation presentation: formulas retain full precision and its money cells display whole dollars. It contains no prefilled worked example, so independently derived formula and boundary cases remain necessary.

The January 2026 guide captures current filing thresholds but assigns exactly $50,000 to both monthly and weekly frequency rows. That boundary requires agency clarification or an explicit Department account assignment.

review.requiredNextStep: Implement the formula and workbook-derived cases in the tax engine, test certificate and residency branches, and resolve the guide's overlapping exactly-$50,000 filing-frequency boundary before automatic filing-frequency assignment.
